title: Functions calling functions
description:
Write `square` first, then build the others on it with `call` (each must call `square`, not multiply on its own):

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `square(x)` | x × x |
| `cube(x)` | x × square(x) |
| `sum_of_squares(a, b)` | square(a) + square(b) |
| `distance2(x1, y1, x2, y2)` | the squared distance (x2 − x1)² + (y2 − y1)² |

Remember: `square` may change any scratch register (`rax`, `rcx`, `rdx`, `rsi`, `rdi`, `r8` to `r11`), so keep what you need across a call in `rbx` or `r12` to `r15`, and save those with `push` and `pop`.

starter.solution.asm:
square:
        mov     rax, rdi
        imul    rax, rdi
        ret

cube:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

sum_of_squares:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

distance2:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
square:
        mov     rax, rdi
        imul    rax, rdi
        ret

cube:
        push    rbx
        mov     rbx, rdi
        call    square
        imul    rax, rbx
        pop     rbx
        ret

sum_of_squares:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        mov     r12, rsi
        call    square                  ; a is already in rdi
        mov     rbx, rax
        mov     rdi, r12
        call    square
        add     rax, rbx
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

distance2:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        mov     r12, rcx
        sub     r12, rsi                ; y2 - y1, kept across the first call
        sub     rdx, rdi
        mov     rdi, rdx                ; x2 - x1
        call    square
        mov     rbx, rax
        mov     rdi, r12
        call    square
        add     rax, rbx
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

rules: Build the others on square with call.
unitTests:
test "square"
    square(9) == 81
    square(-4) == 16
test "cube"
    cube(3) == 27
    cube(-2) == -8
    cube(100000) == 1000000000000000
test "sum_of_squares"
    sum_of_squares(3, 4) == 25
    sum_of_squares(-5, 12) == 169
test "distance2"
    distance2(0, 0, 3, 4) == 25
    distance2(1, 1, 1, 1) == 0
    distance2(-2, 5, 4, -3) == 100
